title: A Scoop of History: How Ice Cream Took Over America
summary: Imagine a frozen treat so beloved that an entire month is dedicated to it! That's exactly what happens every July in the United States. It's National Ice Cream Month, and it all started back in 1984 when President Ronald Reagan said, "Let's celebrate ice cream!" He even made the third Sunday of July National Ice Cream Day. But ice cream's story goes way back. The first people to enjoy something like ice cream were the emperors of China's Tang Dynasty. Their frozen dessert was made with milk, flour, and camphor—a kind of waxy stuff from trees. Much later, in the 9th century, Arab chefs created a more modern version using milk and sugar. Ice cream didn't arrive in America until 1744. That year, Maryland Governor Thomas Bladen served strawberry ice cream at a dinner party. It was a huge hit! Famous early Americans loved it too. George Washington spent about $200 on ice cream in one summer—a fortune back then. Thomas Jefferson even wrote his own vanilla ice cream recipe. But ice was hard to store, so only rich people could enjoy it for a long time. That changed in 1851 when the first ice cream factory opened in Pennsylvania. Suddenly, everyone could get a scoop! Today, Americans eat about 23 pounds of ice cream per person each year. That's like carrying around a heavy bag of dog food made entirely of ice cream! California makes the most ice cream, but people in Rhode Island, Wisconsin, and Washington, DC, eat the most per person. Your favorite flavor might even say something about you. A scientist named Dr. Alan Hirsch found that vanilla fans are often adventurous risk-takers. Chocolate lovers are outgoing and energetic. Strawberry fans are thoughtful and loyal. And if you like mint chocolate chip, you're probably ambitious and confident. Ice cream has also led to some wild world records. In 2014, a dairy in Wisconsin made the world's biggest single scoop. It took 733 tubs of ice cream, weighed 3,010 pounds, and stood over five feet tall—as tall as a refrigerator! Then, in 2023, a shop in Japan created the most expensive ice cream ever. One serving of Byakuya cost $6,696 and included rare white truffles, edible gold leaf, and fancy Japanese cheeses. So, what's your scoop?
why_it_matters: Ice cream is a treat you can enjoy with friends and family, and its long history shows that people everywhere love finding ways to stay cool and happy.

WHAT: The history of ice cream from ancient China to modern records, including National Ice Cream Month and fun facts about flavors and world records.

perspectives.description: Ice cream brings happiness and creates special memories for families and friends, and factories made it affordable for everyone.
Eating too much ice cream can be unhealthy because of the sugar and fat, and some people worry about its environmental impact.
Ice cream's history shows how different cultures contributed to the treat we love today, mixing science, art, and tradition.
